svg.title: Banneret — gems on the party wheel
svg.desc: Layout proposal. The party wheel holds three heroes (Warrior, Skirmisher, Caster). Each hero faces a hero tree wedge (starting colour, then a class keystone and an ascendancy keystone, each revealing the branch beyond it) flanked by four skill wedges: the basic attack and three slots. Coloured gems from the map are the only progression; spent on an empty slot, a skill, or the hero tree. Worked example: the Warrior's Strike evolved into Arcane Strike with a blue gem, and a yellow gem on his hero tree made him a Paladin. Illustrative nodes; no balance values.
svg.text: LAYOUT PROPOSAL · Illustrative nodes, skills and colours; no costs or balance values specified.
Skill wedge, outward: skill · keystone 1 (first form) · keystone 2 (ascended) · keystone 3 on the rim (ultimate)
Hero tree wedge: starting colour · keystone 1 (class) · keystone 2 (ascendancy). Each gem reveals the band beyond it.
Each hero: hero tree + 4 skills (basic attack + 3 slots). Unrevealed bands stay empty.
A blue gem evolved his basic attack. A yellow gem made him a Paladin.
Yellow → Smite · Red → Bash · Blue → Arcane Strike
The blue gem gave 2 blue points, usable in Strike's tree only: two blue nodes bought.
Yellow gem on his hero tree: 5 yellow points, for yellow nodes in any of his trees.
No nodes until the class gem, like a skill.
THREE WAYS TO SPEND A GEM
offers three new skills of that colour
fills its next keystone (form, ascended, ultimate)
2 points of that colour · that skill's tree only
sets the class, later the ascendancy
5 points of that colour · any of that hero's trees
NO GEM IS A DEAD DROP
Warrior's empty slot → choose one of three paladin skills.
Skirmisher's empty slot → no yellow in its kit, so generic yellow skills (e.g. Heal).
Gems are the only progression. Points of a colour buy nodes of that colour.
Node counts, skill names and accepted colours are illustrative.
Ultimate: any colour adds its mechanic · one per hero
